version.changelog: Initial release — log workouts, meals, and weight conversationally via MCP.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: nexus-fitness
Version: 1.0.0

The Nexus skill bundle is a legitimate fitness tracking integration that connects to a remote MCP server (nexus-tad5z6m6za-el.a.run.app). The SKILL.md file provides clear instructions for logging workouts, meals, and weight, as well as managing social connections, with no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's requests and runtime instructions are consistent with a cloud-backed fitness tracker: it is instruction-only, asks users to authenticate via OAuth, and does not request unrelated credentials or system access.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (fitness logging, OAuth cloud storage, conversational queries) lines up with the SKILL.md: it uses a remote MCP endpoint and OAuth for access and exposes tools for log/history/update/friends. Minor mismatch: the README references a CLI install command but the skill has no install spec; this is likely informational rather than a functional requirement but is worth noting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to connect to a single remote MCP endpoint and to prompt the user for Google/Supabase OAuth on first use. It does not instruct the agent to read local files, environment variables, or unrelated system paths, nor to send data to other endpoints. However, the agent will transmit personal fitness and social data to the remote server — confirm you trust that endpoint and its privacy policy before use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — this is an instruction-only skill. That minimizes on-device risk because nothing is downloaded or written by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. The described OAuth flow (user browser sign-in) is consistent with not needing pre-provisioned secrets. No unrelated credentials or system config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-on and uses default agent-invocation behavior. It does not request elevated/persistent system privileges or modify other skills' configuration. Note that autonomous invocation is permitted by default on the platform — combine that with remote data flows only if you trust the service.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for a cloud-backed fitness tracker, but make these checks before installing: (1) Verify you trust the remote endpoint (https://nexus-tad5z6m6za-el.a.run.app) and review the provided Privacy Policy and Terms of Service links and the linked GitHub repo to confirm legitimacy. (2) Understand that signing in via Google/Supabase will grant the server access to user identity and will send your fitness/weight/meal data to that third party — avoid logging sensitive medical data. (3) The SKILL.md mentions a CLI command but there is no install spec in the skill bundle; do not run external install commands unless you verify their source. (4) If you want tighter control, ask the skill owner how OAuth is implemented (what scopes are requested) and whether data can be exported/deleted. If any of these are unclear or you do not trust the endpoints, do not install or use the skill.
